q: Which sectors are approved for the CCTS offset mechanism in phase 1 and phase 2?
title: CCTS offset approved sectors
short: BEE's September 2024 memorandum lists six phase 1 sectors: energy, industries, waste handling and disposal, agriculture, forestry and transport. Phase 2 adds four more: construction, fugitive emissions, solvent use, and carbon capture, utilisation and storage, making ten sectors in all.
audience: Developers deciding whether a project type can enter the Indian Carbon Market

sections.h: Phase 1 sectors and the example technologies BEE gives
ul: Energy: green hydrogen by electrolysis or from biomass, renewable energy with storage, offshore wind, compressed biogas, a more efficient lime kiln.
Industries: green ammonia use, feed switch in integrated ammonia-urea plants.
Waste handling and disposal: biochar, landfill gas capture.
Agriculture: systematic rice intensification, biochar, agroforestry.
Transport: modal shift, electric vehicles and buses.
Fugitive emissions, from fuels and from industrial gases: CF4 reduction in semiconductor plants, recovery and use of gas from oil fields.
Solvent use: no example technology listed.
Carbon capture, utilisation and storage, and other removals: post-combustion CCS.

sections.h: A sector is not a methodology
p: A project also needs an approved methodology. BEE's list had 12 methodologies on 7 July 2026, so many technologies named above still have no method to register under.

senseible: Senseible reads the invoices behind energy and fuel projects; it does not decide sector eligibility.
